title: Globex Media Deal Review
subtitle: Globex Media — Streaming TV, $85K · Lost "Budget cut" · AE: Morgan Lee · Mgr: Dana Chen
footer_left: Sample — fictional data · Deal Review Generator
summary: Recorded loss reason: "Budget cut." An inbound demo request created early momentum, but the champion never secured executive budget sign-off. Facing a mid-year spend freeze, the deal slowly stalled — five close-date pushes over three months in Proposal — while the scope was quietly halved ($140K → $85K) without a reset. It ended as a no-decision, not a competitive loss, which makes it re-engageable next budget cycle.
context: Mid-Market / Direct, new business. Product: Streaming TV. Champion Alex Doyle (Marketing Manager) was enthusiastic but not the economic buyer; the VP of Finance controlled the budget and never joined a call. When a company-wide spend freeze hit in Q2, the un-sponsored deal had no internal advocate senior enough to protect it.

reengage.label: 1 · Re-time to Budget Cycle
reengage.text: The loss was budget timing, not a no. Set a re-engage task now for the next planning window and re-open with a right-sized pilot.

reengage.label: 2 · Multi-Thread to Finance
reengage.text: Get to the VP of Finance early next time — the deal died un-sponsored. Arm the champion with a one-page business case for exec sign-off.

reengage.label: 3 · Lead with a Pilot
reengage.text: Re-approach with a low-commitment pilot and a brand-lift study so value is proven before a full-budget ask.

gaps.label: Gap 1: No Re-Engage Task at Close
gaps.body: A 'Budget cut' loss is highly re-engageable, yet the opp closed with no re-engage task, future date, or next step logged.
gaps.rec: Make a dated re-engage task mandatory in the Closed Lost flow when the reason is budget/timing.

gaps.label: Gap 2: No Executive Sponsor
gaps.body: The deal ran for five months single-threaded on a champion who never had budget authority; the economic buyer never joined a call.
gaps.rec: Require an identified economic buyer to advance past Discovery; block Proposal without a mapped budget owner.

gaps.label: Gap 3: Serial Close-Date Slippage
gaps.body: The close date moved five times over three months, each push keeping the deal 'alive' without a changed commitment.
gaps.rec: Require a reason on every close-date change; auto-flag any opp with 3+ pushes for a qualify-or-kill review.

gaps.label: Gap 4: Happy-Ears Forecast
gaps.body: Probability sat at 60% in Proposal for ~3 months, then dropped to 0% the day it was lost — the forecast never reflected the deal's health.
gaps.rec: Tie probability to objective stage-exit criteria; down-rank stale high-probability opps in the weekly review.

gaps.label: Gap 5: Scope Cut Without Re-Baseline
gaps.body: The amount was halved ($140K → $85K) mid-deal with no reset of plan, timeline, or decision criteria.
gaps.rec: Treat a >25% amount change as a re-baseline trigger — reconfirm scope, timeline, and close plan.

gaps.label: Gap 6: Risk Not Escalated
gaps.body: The champion flagged a spend freeze on the April call, but no manager escalation or save-play was logged before the deal died.
gaps.rec: Log deal risks as tracked items; trigger a manager review when a budget-freeze risk is raised on an active deal.
